name: Brazil 2016-18 (Tite)
scopeNote: Brazil national team under Tite from the first competitive match (World Cup qualifier away to Ecuador, Quito, 2016-09-01, 3-0; NOT October 2016 as in the brief, the Colombia qualifier was 2016-09-06) to the World Cup quarter-final loss to Belgium (Kazan, 2018-07-06, 1-2). Competitions: CONMEBOL qualifiers 2016-17 and World Cup 2018 (17 Jun - 6 Jul); friendlies are context. Tite's appointment date (June 2016, after the Copa America Centenario) is from memory plus a 2016-06-21 africanews headline, not read in the digest, so the 2016-06-20 manager start is unverified. Style term used by sources: 4-1-4-1 (Tite trademark, brought from Corinthians 2015) defending, 4-3-3 in possession with Casemiro as lone pivot, zonal marking (assistant Cleber Xavier to FIFA). WHAT IS DISTINCT (evidence-based): (1) midfield trio of Casemiro (pivot), Renato Augusto (conductor/tempo, left) and Paulinho (late-running shuttler, right), Coach Watch calls it his ideal midfield after 4-1 in Uruguay (2017-03-23); Renato's last start was the 0-0 at Wembley vs England (Nov 2017), after which Tite moved to Coutinho and Willian or Fernandinho (World Football Index; Yahoo); (2) full-backs Dani Alves (right) and Marcelo (left) attacking in triangles with Willian/Paulinho and Neymar/Renato, until pre-World Cup caution; at the World Cup Marcelo/Fagner/Filipe Luis were described as cautious in the Mexico game, (3) Gabriel Jesus as a mobile centre-forward who pressed the build-up (Goal Brasil), Neymar on the left as left-sided playmaker with Coutinho and Marcelo; (4) Tite's own adjustment from a possession-heavy side that struggled against low blocks (Costa Rica, Mexico, Switzerland) toward more width through Willian. Coach Watch (2020) states that in 2019 Tite kept the 4-1-4-1 but used Dani Alves moving inside as a quasi-midfielder in build-up and Firmino as central striker, with full-backs in central areas: that is OUT of this period and is cited only to separate periods, not as verified evidence. WHERE THIN: no tier A/B coverage of the 2016-17 qualifiers (only Coach Watch overview, These Football Times, theScore, Menotti quote); pressing is evidenced mostly by Costa Rica match and Cleber's high/mid/low-press quote, no PPDA or data company numbers; people-management is mostly press and Cleber/Paulinho anecdotes; set pieces covered by Cleber's zonal quote and two press pieces on keeping three men back; the first-18-month squad stability claim (Yahoo) is single-sourced. Popular label 'joga bonito/quadrado magico' (Goal Brasil, 2018) is a press framing; sources show pragmatic structure behind the attackers.
openQuestions: Brief says first competitive match in October 2016; sources show 2016-09-01 (Ecuador away) and 2016-09-06 (Colombia home). Used 2016-09-01.
Tite's start date as manager (June 2016) not read from a mined page; confirm exact day (20 June 2016 from memory).

Number of matches in the period: The Quint says 6 goals conceded in 25 matches before the Mexico game, Goal says 5 goals in 21 matches under Tite at 2018-06-10; counts include friendlies, not reconciled.
Fernandinho 'turned' at midfield and zonal credit: Goal.com and Cleber describe zonal marking, but Lazada 'key takeaways' pages claim it collapsed at set pieces; treated as low-quality and not used.
Dunga/Tite contrasts (theScore 4-3-3 vs Dunga 4-2-3-1) and Menotti '20 metres higher' are single-source claims about line height; no data company confirmation.
Which mid-block/low-block was used vs Belgium (58% possession) is described only by Coach Watch overview and Goal; no dedicated tier A match analysis found for the Belgium game.
